title: Your Dog's Guilty Look Tracked Scolding in a 14-Dog Test 🐶 (Things Living In Your House #65)
description:
Why does your dog look guilty? In a 2009 test of 14 dogs, owners told the dog not to eat a treat and left the room. The "guilty look" was no different whether or not the dog had eaten it. It showed up more when owners scolded, and the effect of scolding was stronger in dogs that had obeyed. In a 2015 study of 96 dogs, owners did no better than chance at telling from the greeting whether their dog had eaten the food. These studies test the look, not what dogs feel.

Sources: Horowitz 2009, Behavioural Processes; Ostojic, Tkalcic & Clayton 2015, Behavioural Processes.
